# PLAN

Design of `rattlerthis`, the `"rattler"` backend of
[`condathis`](https://github.com/luciorq/condathis). It solves, installs and
activates 'Conda' environments inside the R process through the Rust
library [`rattler`](https://github.com/conda/rattler), without a package
manager binary.

History, in short: until October 2026 `rattlerthis` was a front end of its
own (`create_env()`, `install()`, `run()`, `list_envs()`, ..., with its own
root, `RATTLERTHIS_ROOT_DIR` / `rattlerthis.root_dir`, and hand-synced
copies of condathis code), plus an adapter for condathis's first backend
contract. All of that is gone. The move followed a backend spec written
for that work (not in the repository; its work units RT-1 to RT-5 and its
difference IDs such as R-5 are named in these devdocs); this file records
what the package is now.

## What rattlerthis is

- condathis's backend only. Users call condathis's functions with
  `method = "rattler"`; every argument, check, message, result and
  condition class is condathis's, as are `with_sandbox_dir()` and
  `clean_cache()`.
- No exported functions, no options and no environment variables of its
  own. The generic Conda variables `CONDA_OVERRIDE_*` are honored, as
  micromamba honors them.
- `Imports: condathis (>= 0.2.0.9010)`, the version with contract v2;
  `NAMESPACE` imports nothing from it (every call is `condathis::`, so a
  reload of condathis never leaves stale imported closures). condathis does
  not declare rattlerthis: it knows the package from an internal table
  (`known_backend_packages <- c(rattler = "rattlerthis")`) and loads it when
  `method = "rattler"` is used, when `<root>/rattler/envs` has an
  environment, and from `clean_cache()`.
- Registration: `.onLoad()` loads condathis with the version floor read
  from this package's `DESCRIPTION`, calls
  `condathis::register_backend("rattler", new_backend_rattler())`, and
  sets a `packageEvent("condathis", "onLoad")` hook that registers again
  after a reload of condathis. `.onUnload()` removes the hook first, then
  unregisters. A backend object that breaks the contract fails the load.

## Architecture

- **Rust** (`src/rust/`): an `extendr` crate on `rattler`,
  `rattler_conda_types`, `rattler_solve` (pure-Rust `resolvo`),
  `rattler_repodata_gateway`, `rattler_shell`, `rattler_virtual_packages`,
  `rattler_cache` and `rattler_networking`, compiled into the package's
  shared library (`crate-type = ["rlib", "staticlib"]`, linked through
  `src/entrypoint.c`). No `libsolv_c` (no C solver, no `bindgen`).
- **R** (`R/`), about 1,500 lines:
  - `condathis-backend.R`: the backend object, the 7 functions below, and
    registration.
  - `rattler-await.R`: `rattler_await()` (start, poll, cancel and wait for
    a job; spinner), the interrupt handling, and the mapping of Rust error
    kinds to classes.
  - `rattler-env.R`: the root and cache directories, the requests built
    from specs or an `env_file`, the output per verbose level, and the
    activation base environment.
  - `extendr-wrappers.R`: generated by the build (only while
    `ROXYGEN_PKG` is set, see "Build toolchain").

## The backend functions (condathis contract v2)

The object (`c("condathis_backend_rattler", "condathis_backend")`) has the
3 required functions and the 4 optional ones that need rattler:

| Function | Calls |
|---|---|
| `backend_create_env` | `rt_read_env_file()` for an `env_file`, then `rt_install()`, or `rt_install_explicit()` for explicit files (`lock_file = TRUE` for conda-lock files). condathis guarantees the directory is absent and owns the replace/restore life cycle. |
| `backend_install` | `rt_install()`; a missing environment aborts with `rattlerthis_env_not_found`, `condathis_install_packages_env_not_found` and `condathis_env_not_found`. Never creates. |
| `backend_resolve_run` | `rt_activation_env()` against condathis's `base_env` without `CONDA_PREFIX`; returns the changed variables plus `CONDA_DEFAULT_ENV` and `CONDA_PROMPT_MODIFIER`, and the bare command (condathis looks it up). |
| `backend_clean_cache` | `rt_clean_cache()` on `pkgs/` and `repodata_cache/`; `NULL` when neither exists. |
| `backend_quiesce` | waits until `rt_live_jobs()` is 0 (`with_sandbox_dir()` and `clean_cache()` call it before deleting). |
| `backend_native_platform` | `rt_native_platform()`: the platform rattlerthis was built for. |
| `backend_can_solve` | `rt_solve_check()` (repodata only, no package download); `TRUE` for explicit and lock files. Backs condathis's emulation fallback (osx-64 under Rosetta 2, win-64 on Windows on ARM64). |

condathis's defaults supply the rest: `get_install_dir`, `get_env_dir`,
`list_envs`, `env_exists`, `list_packages`, `remove_env` and `available`.
rattler environments are conda prefixes, which the defaults list, read and
remove with micromamba's file-system rules.

## Root and directory layout

```
<condathis root>/rattler/   condathis::backend_root_dir("rattler")
  envs/<env_name>/          conda prefixes (conda-meta/history, records,
                            conda-meta lock, .condathis/backend.json)
  envs/#trash/              condathis's replace and remove trash
  pkgs/                     rattler package cache (.cache.lock, <pkg>.lock)
  repodata_cache/           rattler gateway cache (*.json, shards)
  conda-pkgs/               condathis's: CONDA_PKGS_DIRS of Conda tools run
                            inside rattler environments
```

The root is computed on every call, so `with_sandbox_dir()` moves it, and
nothing creates it but actions and `get_install_dir()`. It lies inside
micromamba's root, but neither backend's `envs/` or caches is inside the
other's.

## Jobs and interrupts

Every long call (solve, download, link, activation, cache cleaning) is a
job on a process-wide `tokio` runtime: `rt_install()` and friends return a
job, R polls it with `rt_job_poll()` and `Sys.sleep()` (2 ms doubling to
50 ms), which R interrupts as usual. Phases: `lock`, `fetch`, `solve`,
`prefetch`, `link`, `activate`, `clean`.

- Ctrl-C cancels the job (`rt_job_cancel()`) and waits until it is idle
  before the interrupt goes on, so no rattler thread writes into a
  directory condathis then restores or deletes. Downloads happen in
  `prefetch`, before the prefix changes; a `link` is never interrupted:
  the wait shows "Waiting for rattler to finish linking, which cannot be
  interrupted." and ignores further interrupts.
- The runtime and the link thread pool are per process and rebuilt after a
  `fork()`: Linux forks (`parallel::mcparallel()`) are fully supported. On
  macOS a forked child cannot use CoreFoundation, so creates, installs and
  HTTP(S) refuse there with a clear error (kinds `link` / `fetch`);
  activation, local solve checks and cache cleaning work.
- An activation's shell is a killable child; it runs with `base_env` as its
  whole environment, `bash` when `base_env`'s `PATH` has it, else `sh`
  (Windows: `cmd`).

## Solving and installing

- Specs are parsed by `rattler_conda_types::MatchSpec`, after the same
  text clean-up as libmamba's; R passes them as read.
- The gateway is queried for `[platform, noarch]`: a channel splits its
  packages between a platform subdir and `noarch` (pip, tzdata and most of
  the Python ecosystem), and the gateway adds neither on its own.
- Channels as micromamba's `--override-channels -c ...`: `channels`, then
  `additional_channels`, then the channel of each channel-qualified spec;
  `defaults` maps to repo.anaconda.com, `nodefaults` is dropped. Installed
  packages are passed as locked (favored) records, so they stay solvable
  without their channels. Priority `strict`, `flexible` or `disabled`.
- As libmamba: `python` pinned to its installed minor version,
  `conda-meta/pinned` honored, `pip` added with `python`, an exclusive lock
  on `conda-meta/conda-meta.lock` during a change, a 10 s connect timeout
  and up to 3 retries.
- After every link, `conda-meta/history` gets micromamba's lines (`+`/`-`
  with the channel URL without trailing slash), without `# cmd:` and
  `# conda version:`; condathis's missing-channels warning reads them.
- Link scripts are not run (`pre-link`, `post-link`, `pre-unlink`); the
  result's `link_scripts_skipped` names them and condathis warns
  (`condathis_link_scripts_skipped`). `activate.d` scripts run.
- `Prefix::create` writes `CACHEDIR.TAG` (and a Time Machine exclusion on
  macOS) in every prefix; kept.
- Environment files (`envfile.rs`, `explicit.rs`) by file name, as
  `micromamba create -f`: environment YAML, explicit (`@EXPLICIT`) and
  plain spec lists, conda-lock (`-lock.yml`). `sel()` selectors follow the
  machine's platform and `${VAR}` in channels is expanded in Rust, both as
  micromamba 2.10.0; `variables:` are ignored, as micromamba does under
  condathis's `--no-env`; mambajs `.json` lock files are read as
  micromamba reads them; `rt_read_env_file()` returns the pip steps
  micromamba would run, and the R side refuses a file that has any
  (`condathis_backend_unsupported`).
- Virtual packages are those of the target platform, with
  `CONDA_OVERRIDE_*` honored, so cross solves (`platform = "osx-64"`) and
  condathis's emulation fallback work.

## Wheel packages

Behind the `wheels` Cargo feature, off by default (see "Vendoring and CRAN
size"): a default build refuses a solve that returns a wheel record with
kind `wheel_unsupported`, and the 2 tests of `test-wheel.R` skip
(`skip_if_no_wheel_support()`, backed by `rt_has_wheel_support()`). These
are the only skips the suite may have.

Channels such as `conda-pypi` publish pure-Python packages as raw `.whl`
files. `rattler_conda_types` models them (`DistArchiveType::Wheel`) and the
solver resolves them, but `rattler::install::Installer` and
`rattler_cache` cannot fetch or link them, so `src/rust/src/wheel.rs` does:

- the solved records are split into conda and wheel records; conda records
  go through `Installer`;
- a wheel is downloaded, extracted (a `.whl` is a zip archive) and placed
  in the environment's `site-packages` by the PEP 427 install scheme
  (`.data/scripts` to `bin`/`Scripts`, `purelib`/`platlib` to
  `site-packages`, `data` to the prefix, `headers` to `include/`);
- `console_scripts` entry points become executables through rattler's own
  `EntryPoint` parser, `python_entry_point_template()` and Windows
  launcher;
- the record is written as a normal `conda-meta/*.json`, so condathis's
  listing and later installs see it like any other package;
- a wheel needs `python` in the same environment.

History: the July 2026 union of the installed packages' channels into
every solve (`channels_with_existing()`) is gone: installed records, wheels
included, are locked records of the solve and need no channel. The
`Installer` now gets every installed record (`with_installed_packages()`,
read without rattler's parallel reader, for fork safety) and the wheel
names in `with_ignored_packages()`; that no longer hits the upstream
`ClobberRegistry` panic ("Expected just reordering") that the July
workaround avoided. The gateway's duplicate-records bug is still worked
around by `dedup_repodata()` (see TODO.md).

## Build toolchain: dev rextendr / dev extendr

`rextendr` is a *build-time* tool only -- it scaffolds `src/`, generates
`R/extendr-wrappers.R`, and templates `Makevars.in`/`Makevars.win.in`. It is
not an `Imports:` and never runs at package load, so tracking its development
version costs nothing at runtime and is invisible to CRAN users. The
templates are vendored into this repo (that's the whole point of
`use_extendr()`), so "upgrading rextendr" means re-syncing those files by
hand.

Synced from rextendr `main` @ `ed3fa0a` (2026-08-21), with the
`extendr-api` crate pinned to extendr `main` @ `74afddc` (2026-07-10 --
still extendr's HEAD as of the 2026-08-28 re-check). Both are pinned to
exact revisions rather than branches, so the build is reproducible and the
vendored tree corresponds to one known commit.

The `ed3fa0a` re-sync brought exactly one change, rextendr #541 ("crate
compiles twice"): the document step is now additionally gated on
`$ROXYGEN_PKG`, which roxygen2 sets only while documenting. Without it,
every dev build rewrote `R/extendr-wrappers.R`; the mtime churn made the
next build treat sources as changed and recompile the whole crate.
Combined here with the existing `@DOCUMENT_FLAG@` gate (upstream has no
CRAN/source-tree-write concern because upstream's gate happens to imply it;
keeping both keeps the two concerns separately visible), and our
exit-status-capturing cleanup is retained rather than upstream's plain
`&&` chain, which skips `rm -f` on failure. Verified both ways: a dev
build without `ROXYGEN_PKG` leaves the wrappers' mtime untouched; with it
set, they regenerate.

What the dev templates change, and why each mattered here:

- **Wrapper generation moved from a Rust `[[bin]]` to a C shim**
  (`src/rust/document.c`, replacing `src/rust/document.rs`). The old
  arrangement ran `cargo run --bin document`, which compiled a *second*
  binary against the entire dependency graph at install time -- on this
  crate graph that is not a cheap step. The new one compiles a ~12-line C
  file and links it against the already-built `librattlerthis.a`, calling
  `write__make_rattlerthis_wrappers()` -- a `#[no_mangle] extern "C"` entry
  point that `extendr_module!` now emits. **This is the reason dev extendr
  is required, not optional**: that symbol does not exist in `extendr-api`
  0.9.0 on crates.io. It also deletes a maintenance hazard -- the old
  `document.rs` carried a hand-copied duplicate of extendr's wrapper-file
  header, which would silently drift from upstream; `write_r_wrappers()`
  now owns that string. Verified byte-identical output before/after.
- **`@WINDOWS_TARGET@` replaces a hardcoded target triple.** The old
  `Makevars.win.in` computed `$(subst 64,x86_64,...)-pc-windows-gnu`
  unconditionally. `tools/config.R` now selects among
  `aarch64-pc-windows-gnullvm` (Windows on ARM64, R 4.6+),
  `x86_64-pc-windows-gnullvm` (Rtools built with clang -- UCRT/LLVM),
  `i686-pc-windows-gnu`, and `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`. This directly
  addresses the UCRT-vs-MSVCRT mismatch risk flagged in an earlier TODO: a CRT
  mismatch surfaces as duplicate symbols or runtime crashes rather than a
  clean link error, so picking the triple from what R was actually built
  with is the fix, not a workaround.
- **Quoted paths throughout** (`"$(CARGOTMP)"`, `--target-dir="..."`).
  Unquoted paths break on any user whose R library or home directory has a
  space in it -- overwhelmingly a Windows problem (`C:\Users\First Last\`).
- **`libgcc_mock` moved from `$(TARGET_DIR)` into `$(CARGOTMP)`**, so it is
  removed by the existing `rm -Rf "$(CARGOTMP)"` cleanup instead of
  lingering in the target dir.

Locally-added on top of the upstream templates (do not drop these when
re-syncing): the `$(NATIVE_LIBS)` capture of rustc's
`--print=native-static-libs` into `PKG_LIBS` -- see the comment block at the
top of `Makevars.in` for why it is required and why hardcoding `-lssl
-lcrypto` would be wrong. And, in `Makevars.win.in`, the vendor marker and
the copy of the import libraries that crates ship themselves
(`windows_x86_64_gnu`, `windows_aarch64_gnullvm`,
`winapi-x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`: `-lwindows.0.48.5`, `-lwinapi_advapi32`,
...) into `$(LIBDIR)`, which R's final link searches. The copy reads the
`cargo:rustc-link-search` directories one per line
(`while IFS= read -r dir`, since 2026-10-28): split on spaces, as before, a
source path with a space (`C:\Users\First Last\...`) copied nothing and the
link failed with `cannot find -lwindows.0.48.5` (reproduced on Windows x64
and in the aarch64-pc-windows-gnullvm cross build).

Note the git dependency does **not** compromise the offline/CRAN story:
`cargo vendor-filterer` vendors git sources like any other, and emits a
matching `[source."git+https://github.com/extendr/extendr?rev=..."]`
replacement stanza. `src/rust/vendor-config.toml` is therefore now
*generated* by `just update-vendor` rather than hand-written -- a
hand-written one missing that stanza fails the offline build. Verified:
`cargo build --offline` against the regenerated tree resolves the git dep
from `vendor/` with no network.

## Vendoring and CRAN size

Current state (measured 2026-11-05): `src/rust/vendor.tar.xz` holds 421
crates, 35.0MB compressed (34,967,928 bytes; 31.8MB and 571MB unpacked on
2026-10-28). The tarball is not in git: see "Releasing the vendored
tarball" below for when it is made and where it goes. Since 2026-10-22,
`just update-vendor` runs `cargo vendor-filterer` once per platform and
merges the trees, keeping a full copy of every crate that a shipped
platform builds (a single multi-platform run had left some of them as empty
stubs). The size history and the policy notes below were written before
that merge.

CRAN's build farm has no network access, so a CRAN release must ship
`src/rust/vendor.tar.xz` (unpacked and used offline via `--offline` +
`CARGO_HOME` pointed at `src/rust/vendor-config.toml` -- see `Makevars.in` /
`Makevars.win.in` / `tools/config.R`). A plain `cargo vendor` of the full
`rattler`-family dependency graph, unfiltered, was 445 crates / 60MB
compressed / **954MB unpacked** -- dominated by things the shipped platforms
never need:

- Multiple major versions of the `windows`/`windows-sys` crate family
  side by side (`windows` 0.48.0 alone was 169MB -- pulled in only by
  `winver`, a tiny transitive dep of `rattler_virtual_packages` used for
  Windows OS-version detection).
- The legacy `winapi` crate's precompiled MinGW import libraries, for
  *both* `x86_64` and `i686` (106MB) -- `i686` Windows hasn't been a CRAN
  target since R for Windows went 64-bit-only.
- `aws-lc-sys` (68MB) -- `rustls`'s default crypto provider bundles a full
  copy of AWS-LC's C/assembly source and needs `cmake`/NASM/Perl to build
  it, an extra native-toolchain requirement beyond a Rust+cargo build that
  CRAN's Windows/macOS machines shouldn't be assumed to have.
- wasm32 (`web-sys`, `wasm-bindgen*`), Android (`jni`), UEFI (`r-efi`), and
  BSD/illumos/Redox-only crates -- none of which `rattlerthis` ever builds
  for.

Four passes cut this to 11.7MB compressed / 150MB unpacked (see the size
table below). The first two, applied together, did most of it -- 412
crates / 14MB compressed / 184MB unpacked (verified at the time:
`cargo build --offline` against the regenerated tree succeeds,
`cargo test --lib` passes with and without `--features wheels`):

1. **`native-tls` instead of `rustls`.** Every `rattler`-family crate that
   touches HTTP (`rattler`, `rattler_repodata_gateway`, `rattler_cache`)
   exposes a `native-tls` feature as a straight alternative to `rustls`
   (`reqwest/native-tls` under the hood), so this needed no patching --
   just flipping the feature flag in `src/rust/Cargo.toml`. `native-tls`
   links the OS's own TLS: Secure Transport on macOS and SChannel on
   Windows (**zero** vendored crypto code on either platform), and system
   OpenSSL via `openssl-sys` on Linux (dynamically linked, not vendored --
   `openssl-sys`'s `vendored` feature is deliberately not enabled). This
   removes `rustls`, `aws-lc-rs`/`aws-lc-sys` or `ring`,
   `rustls-platform-verifier`, `hyper-rustls`, `tokio-rustls`,
   `webpki-root-certs`, and (since `reqwest`'s `http3` feature is only
   reachable through `rustls`) `quinn`/`quinn-proto`/`quinn-udp` -- none of
   which any conda channel needs anyway. The certificates trusted are
   micromamba's (`netenv.rs`): on Linux and macOS the first of libmamba's
   system CA bundles (`/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt`,
   `/etc/ssl/cert.pem`, ...), or `ssl/cert.pem` of condathis's root, only;
   on Windows the system store. A CA only in the macOS keychain is
   therefore not trusted, as micromamba does not trust it either. `SystemRequirements` in
   `DESCRIPTION` should note OpenSSL is needed on Linux (already a de
   facto CRAN-ecosystem requirement -- the `curl` and `openssl` CRAN
   packages need it too).
2. **`cargo vendor-filterer` instead of `cargo vendor`**, restricted to
   the seven triples actually shipped --
   `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`,
   `x86_64-apple-darwin`, `aarch64-apple-darwin`, plus the three Windows
   targets `tools/config.R`'s `.windows_target` can select
   (`x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`, `x86_64-pc-windows-gnullvm`,
   `aarch64-pc-windows-gnullvm`; R for Windows uses Rtools/MinGW, **not
   MSVC**) -- with `--keep-dep-kinds=no-dev` to also drop crates only
   reachable through some dependency's own `[dev-dependencies]`
   (`proptest`, `rusty-fork`, `rand_xorshift`, ...). This alone dropped
   the `windows`-0.48/`winver` chain, all
   `i686`/`windows-msvc`/wasm32/Android/UEFI/BSD-only crates, and every
   duplicate `windows-sys`/`windows` version not needed for the
   `windows-gnu`/`gnullvm` family. `i686-pc-windows-gnu` is deliberately
   *excluded* even though `.windows_target` can name it: `DESCRIPTION`
   requires R >= 4.3 (R dropped 32-bit Windows in 4.2), and including it drags
   back ~52MB of `winapi-i686` import libraries. Adding the two `gnullvm`
   triples cost nothing measurable (still 14MB) -- they share almost all
   their crates with `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`. Regenerate with `just update-vendor` (the
   `justfile` recipe is the single source of truth for the exact command --
   not reproduced here to avoid the two copies drifting apart; it also
   rebuilds `--offline` against the fresh tree, with and without
   `--features wheels`, as a sanity check before you commit). This is not
   automatic -- there is no CI step that detects a stale `vendor.tar.xz`
   yet (see TODO.md). The tarball stays out of git (`.gitignore`): after a
   `src/rust/Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock` change, commit the `Cargo.lock` diff
   only, and regenerate the tarball at the release points of "Releasing
   the vendored tarball" below.
   Vendored for the **default** feature set (no `wheels`) -- that's what
   CRAN ships. `reqwest`/`zip` are already present unconditionally either
   way (see below), so this vendor tree also happens to support a local
   `--features wheels` dev build without regenerating.

3. **Gating `wheels` behind a Cargo feature** (see "Wheel packages"
   above) was applied for scope reasons -- the CRAN release should expose
   only solve/install/activate/run, not the `conda-pypi` wheel-channel
   extra -- but it turned out to save little vendor size: `zip` and
   `reqwest` are already unconditional dependencies of
   `rattler_package_streaming` (the `.conda` package format is itself a
   zip archive) and `rattler_repodata_gateway` respectively, confirmed by
   `cargo tree` showing only a one-crate difference between the two
   feature sets. Kept anyway, since the goal here is a minimal *surface*,
   not just a minimal *tarball*.

4. **Stripping non-compiled crate contents** (2026-08-28) via
   `--exclude-crate-path`: `tests`, `test-macros`, `benches`, `examples`,
   `test-data`/`testdata`/`test_data`, `fuzz`, `ci`, `.github` --
   directories cargo never builds when a crate is compiled *as a
   dependency* (only the lib/build targets are). ~40MB unpacked;
   14MB -> **11.7MB compressed, 150MB unpacked**. The tool rewrites each
   crate's `.cargo-checksum.json`, which is what makes this safe --
   hand-deleting the same files would fail cargo's vendor checksum
   verification. Two lessons encoded in the recipe comments: `*#docs` is
   **not** safe (`fancy-regex`'s lib.rs does
   `#![doc = include_str!("../docs/...")]`, making docs a compile input --
   the recipe's own offline rebuild caught it), and the single biggest win
   was non-obvious (`tracing/test-macros`, 9MB, matched by none of the
   common names -- found by measuring the tree, not guessing).

Size history, all figures measured (compressed = `vendor.tar.xz`;
"pass" numbers refer to the list above):

| state                                   | crates | compressed | unpacked |
|-----------------------------------------|--------|------------|----------|
| plain `cargo vendor`, unfiltered        | 445    | 60MB       | 954MB    |
| passes 1-2 (native-tls + platform filter)| 412   | 14MB       | 184MB    |
| after rattler-family bump (2026-08-28)  | 421    | 14MB       | 190MB    |
| pass 4 (content stripping)              | 421    | **11.7MB** | 150MB    |
| per-platform merge (2026-10-22)         | 421    | 31.8MB     | 571MB    |
| same recipe, re-run (2026-11-05)        | 421    | 35.0MB     | not measured |

### Where this stands with CRAN policy

Checked against the actual policy documents (2026-08-28), because the
folklore here is misleading:

- **CRAN's Rust policy sets no size limit.** It prescribes exactly this
  arrangement -- `cargo vendor`, xz-compressed, offline build, rustc
  version reported before compilation (`tools/msrv.R` does) -- and for
  bundles "too large to be included" its stated remedy is hosting at "a
  long-term secure site under the maintainer's control" with a pinned
  version and an **embedded checksum**. It explicitly says **GitHub does
  not qualify** as reliable hosting, and that downloading should be
  "avoided if at all possible" (CRAN keeps packages installable for
  years).
- **The general policy's 5MB rule is for data and documentation**, not
  source tarballs. The `R CMD check` "installed size" NOTE also does not
  apply: the vendor tree is deleted after compilation (`rust_clean` in
  the Makevars), so the installed package is just the `.so` plus R files.
- **Accepted precedent tops out around 12MB** (CRAN source tarballs,
  measured from CRAN's own servers: `tok` 11.6MB (2026-11-05), `prqlr`
  9.1MB (2026-11-05), `gifski` 6.9MB, `arcpbf` 1.8MB, `orbweaver` 1.1MB,
  `b64` 1.0MB). At 35MB for the vendor tarball alone, ours is about 3x
  the largest known accepted Rust package: well above precedent, still not
  above any written limit. Expect the incoming size flag and a human
  reviewer reading `cran-comments.md`.

### How other Rust packages handle the vendor tarball

Surveyed 2026-11-05: the 94 CRAN packages whose `SystemRequirements` name
cargo or rustc, 88 of whose GitHub repositories could be cloned.

| practice | repos | examples |
|----------|-------|----------|
| `vendor.tar.xz` committed to git, `vendor/` ignored | 61 | `b64`, `b32`, `h3o`, `tomledit` (extendr); `yaml12`, `automerge` (Posit); `tok` (mlverse); `zoomerjoin` |
| tarball in `.gitignore`, made at release time | ~15 | `gifski`, `hellorust` (r-rust); `prqlr`; `tinyimg` |
| tarball downloaded at install from a GitHub release, sha256 checked | 1 | `ggsql` (Posit) |
| unpacked `vendor/` committed | 5 | `fozziejoin`, `scanr` |

The committed tarballs are small: `b64` 0.7MB, `yaml12` 1.3MB, `h3o`
4.5MB, `zoomerjoin` 6.0MB, `automerge` 6.1MB, `tok` 11.0MB. Every update
of a committed tarball keeps a full copy in git history, which is cheap at
that size but not at 35MB per dependency bump (GitHub also warns on files
over 50MB and refuses files over 100MB). `rattlerthis` therefore stays in
the second group. `ggsql`'s GitHub-release download was accepted by CRAN,
but the Rust policy says GitHub is not reliable hosting, so it is not a
pattern to copy.

r-universe builds from git, with network access, so the tarball being in
git or not makes no difference there: all ten packages checked
(`gifski`, `hellorust`, `prqlr`, `tinyimg`, `ggsql`, `b64`, `h3o`,
`yaml12`, `tok`, `zoomerjoin`) build on Windows x64 and Windows on ARM64.
Without the tarball, `Makevars` lets cargo download the crates, as it
does for development builds.

### Releasing the vendored tarball (decided 2026-11-05)

`src/rust/vendor.tar.xz` is a release artifact, not a source file. It is
made with `just update-vendor` only at these points:

- before every CRAN submission or update;
- for every major release of `rattlerthis`.

Between them, git holds `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock` only. Development
builds, CI and r-universe download the crates from crates.io, at the
versions `Cargo.lock` pins.

Each released tarball is also uploaded to Zenodo, as the long-term,
trusted copy: one record, with a new Zenodo version (and DOI) for each
release of the tarball. This meets the Rust policy's remedy for a bundle
"too large to be included" (a long-term site under the maintainer's
control, not GitHub), so the order of preference for a CRAN release is:

1. **Bundle the tarball in the CRAN source package**, with the
   justification in `cran-comments.md`: vendoring is required by CRAN's
   offline rule, the format is the one the Rust policy prescribes, and the
   tree is already platform-filtered, TLS-slimmed and content-stripped
   (60MB unfiltered).
2. **If CRAN refuses the size, download it from Zenodo** at install time,
   with its sha256 embedded in the package sources (see "Checksum tooling"
   below). The Zenodo copy exists from the first release on, so this
   switch needs no new upload.
3. **r-universe** publishes binaries in every case, including Windows on
   ARM64, so users do not need Rust (not yet registered in
   `luciorq.r-universe.dev`; see TODO.md).

### Checksum tooling (planned, not built)

Downloading from Zenodo is only acceptable with a checksum fixed in the
package sources, and nothing does this yet. What the tooling needs to do:

1. **Record each release.** `just update-vendor` (or a separate release
   recipe) writes, next to the tarball, its sha256, its size in bytes,
   the number of crates, and the sha256 of the `Cargo.lock` it was
   vendored from. That ties a tarball to one lock file. A file committed to
   git, for example `tools/vendor-release.dcf`, keeps one entry per
   released tarball: package version, sha256, size, `Cargo.lock` sha256,
   Zenodo record and file URL, DOI.
2. **Hash the uploaded file, not a rebuilt one.** The tarball is not
   reproducible yet: `xz` picks its thread count from the machine's memory
   (the 2026-11-05 run printed "Reduced the number of threads from 4 to 3
   to not exceed the memory usage limit"), and `tar` records file times,
   owners and order. Two runs of the recipe on different machines can give
   different bytes from the same `Cargo.lock`. Until the archive is made
   reproducible (`tar --sort=name --mtime=... --owner=0 --group=0
   --numeric-owner`, a fixed `xz` thread count and preset, and a check that
   two runs give one hash), the recorded sha256 is the one of the file that
   was uploaded.
3. **Check the upload.** A `just verify-vendor` recipe downloads the file
   from Zenodo and checks it against the recorded sha256 and size (Zenodo
   also reports an MD5 per file, as a second check), and that its crates
   match `Cargo.lock`: an offline build from the downloaded tree, as
   `update-vendor` already does for the local one.
4. **Use it at install time.** When `src/rust/vendor.tar.xz` is missing
   and a recorded entry matches the package version, `tools/config.R`
   downloads it from Zenodo and checks the sha256 before unpacking it.
   On a mismatch it stops with an error and never uses the file. When the
   download fails, the build falls back to cargo's own download, which
   only works with network access (not on CRAN's machines, where the
   error must say so). The sha256 needs base R's `tools::sha256sum()` (R
   >= 4.5); `rattlerthis` supports R >= 4.3, so older R needs another way,
   as condathis's checksum of the micromamba download does.
5. **Credit the crates.** The Rust policy also requires the authorship and
   copyright of every vendored crate in the package. `rextendr` has
   `write_license_note()`, which writes a `LICENSE.note` for them; it has
   to be regenerated with each released tarball.

Not pursued (diminishing returns relative to the changes above):

- **`icu_*` Unicode data tables** (pulled in by the `idna`/`url` crates for
  full IDNA hostname support) -- a few MB, not patchable without vendoring
  a modified `idna_adapter` or accepting ASCII-only hostnames, which no
  conda channel needs anyway. Revisit only if size becomes an issue again.
- **Deduplicating remaining crate-version drift** -- real but small
  next to what's above; `cargo tree --duplicates` in CI would catch
  regressions here going forward. The single biggest instance is now
  `rustix` 0.38 + its own 13MB `linux-raw-sys` copy, pinned by
  `async-fd-lock` (a `rattler_repodata_gateway` dependency) -- ~16MB
  unpacked that only an upstream bump can remove.
- **README/CHANGELOG text across crates** (~5MB unpacked aggregate) --
  `--exclude-crate-path` takes exact paths, not filename globs, so this
  would mean hand-listing files per crate; unmaintainable for the savings.
- **Dropping unused *functionality*** (audited 2026-08-28): the only
  functionality in the graph `rattlerthis` categorically never exercises is
  `rattler_menuinst` (Start Menu/.desktop/plist shortcut installation,
  a hard dep of `rattler`) and `rattler_pty` (interactive-shell PTY, a hard
  dep of `rattler_shell`) -- neither is feature-gated upstream, so removal
  would need `[patch.crates-io]` stub crates, and the entire subtree
  (menuinst, pty, plist, quick-xml, known-folders, configparser) measures
  ~2.4MB unpacked / **~0.27MB compressed**. Permanent stub maintenance for
  a quarter megabyte is a bad trade; an upstream feature-gate request to
  `conda/rattler` is the right vehicle if ever revisited. Everything else
  heavyweight is load-bearing: resolvo/petgraph (solver), hyper/reqwest
  (HTTP), zstd/bzip2/zlib (`.conda`/`.tar.bz2` formats), simd-json +
  astral_* (sharded repodata), jiff (repodata timestamps), and the
  per-platform FFI binding crates.

## Results, output and errors

- Create and install return `list(status = 0L, stdout,
  link_scripts_skipped)`: `stdout` holds one line per record of the
  transaction (`+ name version build channel/subdir`, `-` for removals;
  `""` when nothing changed). There is no command line, so condathis
  reports `cmd`, `stderr` and `pid` as `NA`.
- Verbose levels, decided from condathis's strategy string: `"silent"` and
  `"output"` print nothing (condathis prints its own line); `"cmd"` prints
  `Running rattler create <env> -c <channels> <specs>` (or `install`,
  `clean`) to standard output with `cat()`, as `processx` echoes
  micromamba's command line; `"full"` adds the transaction lines; a cli
  spinner shows in interactive sessions at every level but `"silent"`.
- Errors reach R as `"[rattlerthis:<kind>] <text>"` (NUL written as `\0`).
  `rattler_abort()` strips the prefix and aborts with
  `rattlerthis_rattler_<kind>`, `rattlerthis_rattler_error` and
  `rattlerthis_error`; kind `unsupported` also gets
  `condathis_backend_unsupported`. condathis re-raises them as
  `condathis_<fn>_failed` + `condathis_backend_error`, with the rattler
  error as parent. Kinds: `invalid_platform`, `invalid_spec`,
  `invalid_channel`, `invalid_channel_priority`, `virtual_packages`,
  `fetch`, `solve`, `link`, `activation`, `io`, `env_file`, `unsupported`,
  `hash_mismatch`, `wheel_unsupported`, `cancelled`, `internal`.

## Differences from the micromamba backend

Both backends behave the same wherever possible. What a user may notice
is the "Differences from the micromamba backend" section of `?rattlerthis`
(`R/rattlerthis-package.R`); README.md has the short version. The complete
table (each difference with its kind, the test that asserts it, and what
would close it; IDs R-1 to R-42) belongs to the backend spec, which is not
in the repository. Keep all three in step when a difference is closed or
found: a parity test asserts each difference that can be observed on the
test machines.

## CI

- `.github/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml`: ubuntu, macos and windows x64,
  R release. `.github/workflows/win-arm64.yaml`: native ARM64 R on
  `windows-11-arm` (target `aarch64-pc-windows-gnullvm`), plus a check that
  the DLL is ARM64 and imports no toolchain runtime DLL.
- condathis comes from `Remotes` in `DESCRIPTION` (one ref only; pak
  refuses a second ref of the same package in `extra-packages`).
- micromamba 2.10.0 is downloaded and checked by
  `.github/scripts/install-micromamba.sh` and passed as
  `CONDATHIS_MICROMAMBA_PATH` for the parity tests.
- `R CMD check` runs with `--no-tests`; `.github/scripts/run-tests.R` then
  runs the suite once, with `NOT_CRAN=true`, against the installed package,
  and fails unless there is no failure, no error and exactly 2 skips.
- Windows x64 builds with the `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` host toolchain: with
  the MSVC host, cc-rs would cross-compile the C code of `zstd-sys` (the
  only crate of the Windows build with C code; `ring` is only a stale `Cargo.lock`
  entry and is built for no target) with `x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc`, which
  Rtools45 does not ship (expected, not observed). On ARM64 the
  MSVC host works, because rtools45-aarch64 ships
  `aarch64-w64-mingw32-clang`.
- Windows on ARM64 R packages: CRAN has no ARM64 binaries; the workflow
  adds `cran.r-universe.dev`, which has aarch64 binaries for R 4.6 (type
  `windows.binary.clang-aarch64`) of every dependency.
